contract.proves:
Verify the cluster's behaviour when the RBAC service — and therefore the
resource-info lookup that scopes authorization — is unavailable.

WHY THIS EXISTS

Until 2026-08-14 the gRPC interceptor handled a failed resource-info lookup by
logging a warning, substituting an empty resource-info slice, and CONTINUING
into authorization:

    resource lookup fails -> warning -> resources = [] -> action check runs
                          -> request may proceed WITHOUT resource scope

The action-level permission check still ran, so this was never a total bypass.
What was silently dropped was the per-resource binding: a caller was evaluated
as though the method touched no resources at all, precisely when authorization
data was least trustworthy (RBAC restarting, slow, or partitioned).

Commit 01bc3e9c changed it to deny:

    resource lookup fails -> authorization scope unknown -> DENY

That is the correct security direction, and it creates a specific operational
risk worth testing rather than assuming: a latent RBAC reliability problem that
used to be invisible now becomes visible as denied RPCs. The interceptor is
reached through the shared globular_service lifecycle by most services, so this
is a platform-wide semantic change, not a single-service one.

WHAT THIS SCENARIO CAN AND CANNOT ASSERT — read before trusting a green run

CAN:
  - the cluster survives RBAC being unavailable without cascading failure
  - RBAC re-registers and the cluster returns to healthy afterwards
  - no ERROR-severity doctor findings persist once RBAC is back
  - service logs are collected so the denial signature can be inspected

CANNOT (harness limitation, not a design choice):
  - assert an allow/deny VERDICT. The authz.check probe currently proves only
    that the authz layer is reachable — smoke/authz-basic states this plainly:
    "proves the authz infrastructure is present, not that it makes the right
    decisions". Asserting a verdict needs the gRPC-level ValidateAccess check
    the security suite has declared as future work.

Until that exists, the canary predicate below must be checked BY A HUMAN in
the collected logs. Write it down here so the check is not reinvented:

    expected during normal operation:   no occurrences
    expected while RBAC is down:        resource-info lookup failed for <method>
                                        (authorization scope unknown)

Zero unexpected occurrences of that signature during NORMAL operation is the
strong evidence. General cluster health staying green is the weak evidence —
health can stay green while scoped authorization quietly denies a minority of
calls.

THE ASSERTION THAT MATTERS MOST IS THE NEGATIVE ONE

An unmapped method must still pass through. getActionResourceInfos converts a
"not found" into an empty result with a NIL error, so only genuine failures
reach the deny path. If that classification is ever removed, denying on error
would start rejecting every unmapped method and take the platform down. The
unit-level guard for this lives in
services/golang/interceptors/resource_scope_failclosed_test.go; this scenario
is the cluster-level companion, and it is the reason the fix is safe to ship
at all.
